brief_extract: The chief impression one gets on approaching the house is its wonderful setting, the wooded background sweeping down the hillside, the rippling river and terraced green of fine pasture. Yet this setting is not natural, as one would suppose, but was the work of England's outstanding landscape artist, Capability Brown, who in the 18th century rendered picturesque the barren and forbidding Derwent Valley. The house itself is full of works of art that are a tribute to both the taste and wealth of generations of the Cavendish family who have lived there.

title: King
brief_context: His coronation required the use of the new vacuum cleaner.
brief_extract: The machine stood at the kerbside and the dust was sucked out from the carpets and furniture in the house through long hoses which were brought in by the company's men, generally through first-floor windows. At the time of the Coronation of King Edward VII, when all the preparations in the Abbey were finished, it was found that the pile carpets under the two thrones were dusty and dirty and time did not allow for their removal for cleaning. A machine was rushed to the Abbey, the hoses led in and in a short time the cleaning was well accomplished.

title: Queen
brief_context: Present at a vacuum cleaner demonstration at Buckingham Palace.
brief_extract: A machine was rushed to the Abbey, the hoses led in and in a short time the cleaning was well accomplished. The King later commanded a demonstration at Buckingham Palace, which was carried out in his presence and that of Queen Alexandra. The popularity of the vacuum cleaner spread rapidly, and theatres, large hotels, etc., put in their own installations, one of the earliest being the Houses of Parliament.

brief_extract: Branch, of which I am a member, held a Home Electricity Course, I readily accepted the opportunity to learn more.
